h: The Menorah and the Crown of the Oral Torah

p: "Speak to Aharon and say to him:
toward the face of the Menorah
shall the seven lamps give light.
toward the face of the Menorah
Besides the fact that the whole pasuk
for it is obvious that he fulfilled Hashem's command
it would suffice to write "And Aharon did so,"
shall the seven lamps give light."
וְזֶה מַעֲשֵׂה הַמְּנוֹרָה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ח, ד)
"And this is the work of the Menorah," etc. (Bamidbar 8:4)
all of it has no connection
to the subject of the parshah.
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיַּעַשׂ כֵּן אַהֲרֹן
on what is said, "And Aharon did so,"
that he was the one who lit,
which alludes to a supernal matter
and perhaps it was hinted to him
Aharon and his sons shall arrange it
And it appears that there is alluded there
But from where was it hinted to him
that he should light it himself,
when it explicitly says "Aharon and his sons"?
And in its plain sense it appears
that he inferred it from its saying "yaaroch,"

p: "'And it is like a groom coming out of his canopy,' etc.
with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding" (Shir HaShirim 3:11).
(end of Parshas Pekudei and elsewhere; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:11):
until He called them 'My mother,'" etc.,
And afterward in the holy Zohar:
דָּא הוּא רֵישָׁא דְּכָל נְהוֹרָא וְכוּלֵּי
this is the head of all light," etc.
as written in the holy Zohar
that Zeir Anpin is the name for
that they will attain in the future;
and in this world there merited this
Moshe Rabbeinu and those like him.
And this is the matter of what is said:
for the sun is the Holy One, blessed be He,
and the moon is Knesses Yisrael,
we call it the Oral Torah
And this is what the Midrash says
was handed over to the Sages,
as in "My children have defeated Me"
"For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge,
and they seek Torah from his mouth,"
And this is what is said:
as it were, Hashem, may He be blessed.
And this is what the Ramban wrote,
that it alludes to a supernal matter
as it were, Hashem, may He be blessed,
"With the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding."
"And Hu is like a groom coming out of his canopy"
that is, on the day of his wedding;
crowns the Holy One, blessed be He,
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him."
And this is Aharon's main occupation,
only it was made valid also through his sons.
And this is what is said:
the aspect of the Written Torah
that is, the essence of the mitzvah,
which shines forth in the heart,
in the manner of what is said:
"And you shall say in your heart"
that is, that there will shine in his heart
the power of "Come and give Me light,"
which is the power of the Oral Torah
And this is why the expression "to him" (eilav) is used,
and it does not say "and say lo":
means that it is designated to him alone,
that it is particular to his power.
although it was made valid through his descendants,
he did it himself all the days of his life,
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote.

p: toward the face of the Menorah
shall the seven lamps give light";
According to this it is difficult:
הָיָה פּוֹנֶה אֶל מוּל פְּנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה
faced toward the face of the Menorah,
And according to the view that
they were placed east to west,
for the second lamp is called the western lamp;
but according to the view that
they were placed north to south,
that the middle one faced west
and the six faced the middle lamp;
for the six faced the middle one,
Why not turn all of them
for they correspond to the six workdays,
which are the preparation for the holiness of Shabbos
And according to the view that
they were placed north to south,
so that the middle one is the western lamp,
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּגִיטִין
it is in the manner of what is written in Gittin (77a),
and three days after Shabbos are reckoned.
And this is what is said afterward:
that he himself was the one who lit,
because this is particular to his power:
who said to him with the words "and say to him":
that this power is particular to him,
to radiate also into all of Yisrael,
the power of the Oral Torah:
And this is what is said afterward:
"And this is the work of the Menorah:
and as written in the Sifrei,
that Moshe had difficulty with it.
the root of the Written Torah,
as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He
that this power is in Aharon,
and he will radiate this power
And this is what is said: "And this";
for the height of the Menorah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
That is, the vav of the word,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא)
(as written in the holy Zohar, beginning of Parshas Vayikra);
and this is the aspect of the Written Torah,
for the Holy One, blessed be He,
corresponding to the twelve tribes of Yah,
which is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah
vav is the Holy One, blessed be He,
(as written in the holy Zohar many times),
in the work of the Menorah,
there is alluded an exalted secret:
"with the crown with which his mother crowned him";
those who impart to the Holy One, blessed be He,
כְּעִנְיַן לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא (דְּבָרִים ל, יב)
as in "It is not in Heaven" (Devarim 30:12);
therefore they are called with the word "zeh,"
And this is what is said of the middle lamp,
which corresponds to the attribute of Malchus,
up to its base, up to its flowers,
that Moshe had difficulty with this,
as it were, to Hashem, may He be blessed,
as in the parable of the sighted man and the blind man
(brought in Midrash Rabbah on this parshah, Bamidbar Rabbah 15:5);
the aspect of the Written Torah,
he knew nothing of this at all;
"According to the vision that He showed,
from the root of the Oral Torah.
that the Holy One, blessed be He, made it:
the essence of the Oral Torah
is from the dew of Atika,
which Hashem, may He be blessed, causes to shine
in the hearts of the Sages;
only it is not apparent to them,
that it is newly produced from their own minds;
which drips from Hashem, may He be blessed,
into the hearts of the Sages;
it is called by their name,
as if they were the innovators,
as it were, Hashem, may He be blessed,
